lead: Sudden collapse in labour, at delivery or soon after, when amniotic fluid and fetal cells enter the mother's blood. Rare (1 in 8 000–30 000), unpredictable, not preventable, often fatal. Timing: 70% in labour around ROM · 19% at caesarean · 11% after delivery.
f: Induction, ARM, strong contractions (oxytocin) · Caesarean, instrumental delivery · Multiple pregnancy, polyhydramnios · Older mother, eclampsia · Placenta praevia, abruption · Cervical laceration, uterine rupture

An anaphylactoid reaction, not a mechanical block · Phase 1 (minutes): pulmonary vasospasm, right heart failure, hypoxia, collapse · Phase 2 (within 4 h): DIC and massive bleeding · Only 12% have DIC at the start; almost all survivors develop it

Warning: sudden breathlessness, chills, agitation, "something is wrong" · Severe dyspnoea, cyanosis, hypoxia → respiratory arrest · Hypotension, arrhythmia → cardiac arrest · Convulsions, coma · Fetal bradycardia · Then bleeding from uterus, wound, cannula sites: blood will not clot

sc: Breathless and cyanosed minutes after ARM on oxytocin, then a fit → Amniotic fluid embolism

f: None proves AFE: send while resuscitating · ABG: hypoxia, acidosis · Clotting: PT, aPTT up, fibrinogen down, D-dimer up · Bedside clot test: no clot in 7–10 min · CXR: pulmonary oedema · ECG, echo: right heart strain · Diagnosis is clinical, by exclusion · Squames in PA blood: supportive only · Definitive: fetal squames in lung vessels at post-mortem

tr: Never wait for clotting results: use the clot test and give blood products

f: PE: postnatal, pleuritic pain, swollen calf, no early DIC (CTPA, heparin) · Eclampsia: high BP, fit first, SpO₂ normal (MgSO₄ 4 g IV) · Haemorrhage: blood loss before shock · Anaphylaxis: after a drug, rash, wheeze (adrenaline 0.5 mg IM) · Local anaesthetic toxicity: after an epidural top-up (lipid 20% 1.5 mL/kg) · MI, septic shock, aspiration

sc: Day 5 after CS, pleuritic pain, swollen calf → Pulmonary embolism
Collapse 10 min after IV ampicillin, urticaria, wheeze → Adrenaline 0.5 mg IM

f: Save the mother first; never wait to prove the diagnosis · Phase 1: O₂ 15 L/min, intubate early · left tilt or push the uterus left · fluids with care (right heart failing) · low BP after fluids: vasopressor ± inotrope · CPR 30:2 · Phase 2: blood + FFP 15 mL/kg · cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen < 2 g/L · platelets if < 50 · TXA 1 g IV · atony: oxytocin infusion, carboprost 250 µg IM · still bleeding: hysterectomy

tr: Giving 3 L of fluid fast overloads the lungs through the failing right heart

f: Cardiac arrest at ≥ 20 wk (fundus at or above the umbilicus), no output after 4 min of good CPR · Start at 4 min, baby out by 5 min · Where she lies: no transfer, no consent, CPR continues · Purpose: uterus off the IVC and aorta so CPR works: mainly for the mother

sc: Cardiac arrest at 36 wk, no output after 4 min of CPR → Perimortem caesarean where she lies
Cardiac arrest at 16 wk → CPR only, no perimortem caesarean
tr: Moving her to theatre for the caesarean wastes minutes and stops CPR

f: Maternal death 13–80% · up to 85% of survivors have hypoxic brain damage · High perinatal death · Recurrence rare; next delivery in a hospital with ICU · Report for maternal death review
